instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of 'legislative agent' and 'engage/engagement' is based on being engaged to actively advocate (with 'engage' meaning employed or retained for compensation) and contains no dollar compensation threshold that triggers registration.

Registration is required for each legislative agent and employer after an engagement, and the statute defines legislative agent by purpose/time rather than by any expenditure amount, so no lobbyist-definition expenditure threshold exists.

A 'legislative agent' is defined as an individual engaged during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes, but no quantitative time magnitude or unit is specified.

Meal and food/beverage expenditures by a legislative agent only become itemized once they exceed $50 aggregated per calendar year for a particular covered official/employee, establishing a de minimis threshold for that category of itemized reporting.

Legislative agents and employers must file updated registration statements and accompanying expenditure/financial-transaction statements on the statutory schedule without any exemption for low total expenditures, so any amount triggers the filing duty once registered/engaged.
Although the legislative-agent definition refers to 'at least a portion' of time and 'main purposes,' the statute provides no percentage-of-compensated-time exemption threshold for filing.
